subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should the Telegram plugin add a public channel/account parse-mode or text-mode config, and which modes/defaults should it support across durable sends, captions, edits, and streaming previews?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this would add a public Telegram config contract that changes rendering, escaping, rich-message compatibility, and security semantics.

options.title: Add Narrow Plain/HTML Contract
options.body: Support the current HTML-compatible default plus an explicit plain/no-parse mode with account inheritance and full outbound-funnel coverage.

options.title: Add Broader Rich/MarkdownV2/Entity Modes
options.body: Expose more formatting choices, accepting a larger API, escaping, compatibility, and security review across MarkdownV2, raw HTML, rich messages, and entity semantics.

options.title: Decline Parse-Mode Config For Now
options.body: Keep the existing richMessages and markdown.tables knobs and continue fixing formatter-specific issues without adding another public config surface.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Plain/HTML Contract
recommendation.body: Support the current HTML-compatible default plus an explicit plain/no-parse mode with account inheritance and full outbound-funnel coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the original HTML-formatting decision and prior parse-mode product review context.
